2. Working With the Agent

For Question 4, the agent’s first query showed that GPU cloud was the only expense category above average. I wanted to understand where the $11,874.30 average came from, so I added a cell called q4_category_totals to show the spending for all four categories. The four totals added up to $47,497.19. Dividing by four gave me $11,874.30, rounded to the nearest cent. With all four amounts visible, I could see that only GPU cloud, at $36,733.93, was above that average. See my Question 4 commit.

3. Reading It Back

I am picking Q7 from the list: “Every task checked against the rule that its assignee works on its project, and a list of any that break it.” I chose Question 7 because I want to check whether each assigned task goes to someone who works on that project. I expect the joins to return 300 rows before I filter or group the results. I start with 300 tasks. For each task, I look up the assigned employee and check whether they belong to that project. Each task can match at most one employee and one membership for that employee on that project. Since I’m using LEFT JOIN, I keep the task even if either match is missing. That leaves me with one row per task.

Each task could match at most one employee and one membership for that employee on that project, so no task appeared twice. After filtering, each row represents one task assigned to someone who was not a member of that project. Tasks 299 and 300 both appeared because they are two separate tasks, even though both were assigned to Omar Said on project 1.
